papers.title: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ Circuits
papers.abstract: Torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one, were proposed by Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao as a route to $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ lower bounds. We prove degree upper bounds for torus polynomials approximating a function on every input. First, for every $\epsilon\in(0,1/4)$, $\mathsf{AND}_n/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, improving the previous $O(\log^2(n/\epsilon))$. This is optimal up to constant factors for inverse-polynomial error, by a lower bound of Krishan and Vishwanathan, and refutes two superlogarithmic-degree conjectures of Krishan and Sarma. Second, for every Boolean function $g$ computed by a depth-$d$, size-$s$ $\mathsf{AC}^0[m]$ circuit, $g/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree at most $C_m^d(\log s)^{\max\{1,\mu-1\}d}\log(1/\epsilon)$, where $\mu$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $m$ and $C_m$ depends only on $m$. This improves the bound $(\log s)^{O_m(d^2)}(\log(1/\epsilon))^{O_m(d)}$ of Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao, making the exponent of $\log s$ linear in the depth and the dependence on $\log(1/\epsilon)$ linear. Both proofs sample terms of a Fourier expansion and approximate them by low-degree torus polynomials. A torus approximation of degree $D$ can be written as a linear combination of at most $(n+1)^D$ parities, called a periodic Fourier representation, which is known to give a non-adaptive measurement-based quantum computation with linear side-processing using one qubit per parity. Hence every $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ function can be computed with quasipolynomially many qubits and inverse-polynomial error probability on every input. Conversely, we prove that a periodic Fourier representation with $r$ parities and error probability $\epsilon$ gives a torus approximation of degree $O(\log(r/\epsilon))$, so the two notions are equivalent.

papers.title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1
papers.abstract: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of H\"aner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. With generic post-processing and the baseline's window costs, splitting alone then shrinks the largest run at most 1.86 times within the budget. To gain more, we make each exponent bit cheaper with windows that share one table point among exponent values related by six symmetries of the curve, on a point-addition core borrowed from the ECDSA.Fail leaderboard. One random scalar and one random start per run give every approximate addition uniform operands, and a bound on each run's outcomes certifies, for every key, a decoder that discards flagged runs. We count every Toffoli gate and every qubit of every run, and each configuration solved all 563 of its pre-registered simulated trials on secp256k1. The best one shrinks the largest run 3.87 times at 8.79 times the baseline's total volume, against 2.81 times for Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff on the same core, and its run is at least 2.6 times smaller than every design of Initio Intelligence.

papers.title: Large-Scale Streaming Portfolio Optimization with Pauli Correlation Encoding
papers.abstract: Classical portfolio construction over large asset universes is a combinatorial selection problem that existing heuristics do not solve well at scale. Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) addresses this by representing the underlying clustering problem with far fewer qubits than one per asset, and a prior study showed it is competitive with classical methods on a single historical snapshot. This paper moves beyond that static test to a streaming deployment, in which the correlation structure and the portfolio are both re-estimated on a rolling basis, as a live rebalancing system would actually operate. We introduce two streaming variants -- PCE itself and a joint multi-cut variant, dPCE -- and evaluate both against a Buy & Hold baseline across window lengths, portfolio sizes up to several thousand assets, risk-aversion and transaction-cost settings, and measurement-shot budgets. Streaming PCE and dPCE consistently outperform the passive baseline, including during a market downturn where both lose money but PCE loses markedly less -- evidence that the method's value is not confined to rising markets. PCE also proves the more practical choice at scale, since dPCE's resource requirements and its sensitivity to rebalancing frequency both grow faster with portfolio size. We further report which operational choices -- rebalancing cadence, shot budget, and transaction-cost awareness -- matter most for a real deployment, and which matter less than commonly assumed.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-B\'enard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.

papers.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
papers.abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.

papers.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
papers.abstract: The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods. Nonetheless, theoretical evidence for or against such an advantage remains scarce. Here, we investigate this in sparse random non-local Hamiltonians. We design a classical algorithm for such Hamiltonians that enables accurate computation of spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision $\varepsilon$, our algorithm runs in time $(1/\varepsilon)^{2+o(1)}$, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. Crucially, this applies even at late evolution times, low temperatures, and near critical points, where existing classical methods require exponential time. Rather than directly simulating a quantum state or operator, our algorithm first computes the model's mean behavior and then a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections. These corrections predict long-time behavior based on short-time data using free probability theory.

papers.title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
papers.abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification with a known ideal success fraction, under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.

papers.title: The Capacity of Conference Key Agreement over GHZ Networks
papers.abstract: $K$ users share independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of the users, and want a common secret key, using local operations and public classical communication (LOCC). We show that the conference key capacity, the largest number of secret key bits per copy of the resource, equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state. Measuring first is therefore optimal, even when the users keep quantum memory and communicate over any number of rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity, the largest number of GHZ states shared by all users obtainable per copy.

papers.title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.

papers.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known. For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, which include all qubit stabilizer codes of this kind, we determine when the bound holds and how far it can fail. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. If this number is less than twice the number of logical qudits, the bound holds, also for degenerate codes. If it is exactly twice that, the bound overstates the number of pairs by at most the length of the longest classical maximum distance separable (MDS) code of that dimension, minus the dimension. Codes carrying values and derivatives of polynomials on the projective line attain this maximum whenever the field size is at least that dimension and the MDS conjecture is known for it, which includes every prime and, by a recently announced result, every even field size. If the number is more than twice the number of logical qudits, the violation is bounded in terms of the lengths of classical codes of a given Singleton defect, and the bound is attained for one logical qudit. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
papers.abstract: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.

papers.title: Quantum Community Detection for Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Community detection offers an alternative to conventional methods for data analysis tasks such as feature selection and clustering, and detecting communities with quantum algorithms is a promising avenue for quantum speedup. We investigate quantum spectral community detectors, such as the modularity-matrix algorithm deteQt, in pipelines for both tasks. We first generalise deteQt to multiple communities by recursive bisection, and show that it recovers planted communities, and hence redundant features, in synthetic and small datasets. We then propose projeQt, which applies a spectral filter to the encoded modularity matrix through the quantum singular value transformation, retaining higher-order eigenvectors that deteQt does not use. projeQt acts on the generalised modularity matrix and extracts several communities at once, without recursion, by k-means clustering of a Gram matrix built from quantum state overlaps. On MNIST we demonstrate both pipelines, selecting informative pixels and classifying images directly by clustering, and find them competitive with standard community detectors.

papers.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method. We model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks in the output distribution. These models guide both the generation of synthetic training data and the design of a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain that attenuates or amplifies higher retained Fourier modes. We score each candidate order by averaging the correlations between its ideal distribution and the distributions measured in three circuit executions. The network adjusts these scores to guide the order estimate and determine the weights of a normalized mixture of the ideal distributions. On 1,351 simulated test cases for general modular exponentiation, held out by circuit configuration, exact order recovery rises from 19% to 34%, and the median Jensen-Shannon divergence from the ideal distribution falls by 50%, from 0.64 to 0.32. On 101 Mersenne rotation circuits executed across five IBM quantum processors, a separate model trained and calibrated in simulation increases the number of correct order estimates from 35 to 53. Algorithmic structure can remain recoverable even when noise makes it barely visible.

papers.title: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured
papers.abstract: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible. We report three active benchmarks, all exact classical statevector simulations of 8-qubit fidelity kernels with no quantum component in the inference path: a sample-efficiency sweep on Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer at ten training-set sizes; raw-versus-processed arms on 1,200 M-SYNTH simulated mammograms with a matched closed-form dequantisation surrogate, five classical methods at the same input and eleven kernel families; and a 30-seed selection-inflation measurement on BreastMNIST. A CMMD D1 clinical arm is withdrawn as a result arm because its frozen splits leak the label through patient serial order, a defect reported in a separate study; it is retained only as a worked example. All three active arms are negative. On M-SYNTH raw an apparent +0.1736 (p = 5.2e-06) against a tuned RBF-SVM falls to +0.0019 (p = 0.937) against a random forest at the same input, and a Laplacian kernel wins on validation. On WDBC, with model selection confined to training data, the quantum kernel is below the selected classical arm at every training-set size, with 2 of 200 paired subsamples ahead. Best-of-30 seed selection adds +0.0210 on BreastMNIST. One result does not fit: at bandwidth 2pi the matched closed-form Gaussian surrogate failed to reproduce the M-SYNTH raw kernel (0.5410 against 0.7045, p = 6.3e-06). Comparator choice and selection each produce effects larger than any quantum-classical difference we measured; we give a reporting standard that removes both.

papers.title: A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression
papers.abstract: For a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, we determine when the Holevo rate is achievable with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. In the maximal Koashi--Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble, this occurs exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits, this means that the signals are all pure or commute pairwise. If any occupied quantum part is mixed, every code with sufficiently small mean local error has rate bounded away from the Holevo information, uniformly in blocklength. To prove the converse, we apply Fawzi--Renner recovery to a hypothetical sequence of visible codes approaching the Holevo rate at vanishing local error, then invoke a decoupling bound of Baghali Khanian and Winter for blind compression.

papers.title: Bare-ancilla fault-tolerant syndrome extraction: General extensions of distance-three codes and structural criteria for graph codes
papers.abstract: The reliability of quantum computation critically depends on the performance of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs). Performance of QECCs can be severely degraded by hook errors, which effectively reduce the code distance. We develop a systematic framework for bare-ancilla syndrome extraction in $[[n,k,3]]$ stabilizer codes. It provides a criterion for a specific single ancilla fault model and jointly searches for suitable stabilizer generators and data-ancilla interaction orders to correct hook errors. We call such stabilizer generator sets bare-ancilla codes (BACs). We also present two constructions that enlarge the set of valid BACs while preserving minimum distance, either by keeping the number of logical qubits fixed or by increasing it. Under the correlated-data error model, $3177$ $[[7,1,3]]$ graph codes are found to be BACs out of $3379$ and all $335415$ $[[8,1,3]]$ graph codes are BACs. We tested $500$ $[[7,1,3]]$ and $1000$ $[[8,1,3]]$ graph codes in the presence of anisotropic and depolarizing noise. The number of data-ancilla interactions is an important predictor of the pseudo-threshold of these graph codes. In the analyzed codes, the BAC, which works with the bare ancilla method, usually performs well or better than the flag method, particularly for depolarizing noise. Notably, we report new bare ancilla codes, namely $[[6,1,3]]$ and $[[7,1,3]]$ with improved code rate compared to the bare code used in the work of Muyuan Li \emph{et al.} and Maheshwari \emph{et al.} respectively.

papers.title: Adaptive Microwave Reception with Diamond Spin Sensors
papers.abstract: In a diamond-spin microwave receiver, pilot measurements can identify the spin-control phase that best separates binary phase-shift keyed symbols. Applying that phase takes time, during which carrier drift can erase the gain in alignment. We derive an exact feedback-delay threshold for a single payload spin from the phase information in the pilot record. On a finite menu of control phases, the pilot record enters the minimum-error update decision only through the direction of its first circular moment when that moment is nonzero. This result motivates a controller that estimates the direction from orthogonal pilot measurements and retains the existing phase whenever the predicted gain is lost to diffusion. For finite spin ensembles, we bound the distinguishability of the photon-count distributions in terms of optical readout and carrier-phase uncertainty, including fluctuations shared across spins. Packet simulations at matched spin budgets show that gated feedback can improve reliability with a single readout channel. With independently readable quadratures and sufficient spin preparations, decision-directed software tracking achieves lower packet error without a hardware phase update.

papers.title: Instance-optimal high-precision shadow tomography with few-copy measurements: A metrological approach
papers.abstract: We study the sample complexity of shadow tomography in the high-precision regime under realistic measurement constraints. Given an unknown $d$-dimensional quantum state $\rho$ and a known set of observables $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$, the goal is to estimate expectation values $\{\mathrm{tr}(O_i\rho)\}_{i=1}^m$ to accuracy $\epsilon$ in $L_p$-norm, using possibly adaptive measurements that act on $O(\mathrm{polylog}(d))$ number of copies of $\rho$ at a time. We focus on the regime where $\epsilon$ is below an instance-dependent threshold. Our main contribution is an instance-optimal characterization of the sample complexity as $\tilde{\Theta}(\Gamma_p/\epsilon^2)$, where $\Gamma_p$ is a function of $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$ defined via an optimization formula involving the inverse Fisher information matrix. Previously, tight bounds were known only in special cases, e.g. Pauli shadow tomography with $L_\infty$-norm error. Concretely, we first analyze a simpler oblivious variant where the goal is to estimate an observable of the form $\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i O_i$ with $\|\alpha\|_q = 1$ (where $q$ is dual to $p$) revealed after the measurement. For single-copy measurements, we obtain a sample complexity of $\Theta(\Gamma^{\mathrm{ob}}_p/\epsilon^2)$. We then show $\tilde{\Theta}(\Gamma_p/\epsilon^2)$ is necessary and sufficient for the original problem, with the lower bound applying to unbiased, kurtosis-bounded estimators when $p \geq 1$. Our upper bounds rely on a two-step algorithm combining coarse tomography with local estimation. Notably, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ob}}_\infty = \Gamma_\infty$. In both cases, allowing $c$-copy measurements improves the sample complexity by at most $\Omega(1/c)$. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between quantum learning and metrology, unifying asymptotic metrological limits with finite-sample learning guarantees.

papers.title: Minimum-Length Permutation-Invariant Qudit Codes from Edge-Colorings of Complete Graphs
papers.abstract: We study permutation-invariant quantum codes in the symmetric subspace $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ of $n$ qudits of local dimension $q$. For every integer $q\ge 2$, we construct a permutation-invariant code with parameters $((4,q,2))_q$. Thus four physical qudits suffice to encode one logical qudit with distance two in the symmetric sector for every local dimension. We also show, using a self-contained decoupling and rank argument, that no permutation-invariant code of dimension $q$ and distance at least $2$ exists in $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ for $n\le 3$. Hence four qudits are necessary and sufficient. The construction has simple representation-theoretic and combinatorial descriptions. On $\mathrm{Sym}^4(\mathbb{C}^q)$, the distance-two Knill--Laflamme conditions split into root and Cartan parts. By restricting supports to the even-entry occupation layer, all root-error conditions vanish automatically. The remaining Cartan conditions reduce to linear balancing constraints on packets of occupation vectors. These packets admit a natural graph-theoretic interpretation in terms of the vertices and edges of the complete graph $K_q$: for odd $q$, they are organized by the midpoint rule, while for even $q$, they are organized by a decomposition of $K_q$ into perfect matchings. In this way, the existence of minimum-length $((4,q,2))_q$ permutation-invariant codes is reduced to a parity-dependent edge-coloring problem on $K_q$.

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.

papers.title: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
papers.abstract: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.

papers.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
papers.abstract: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.

papers.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
papers.abstract: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. However, we show that three-photon sources can produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. To prove this, we view the three paths fed by each source as an edge of a $3$-uniform hypergraph, so that accepted emission patterns correspond exactly to perfect matchings. We construct such hypergraphs with arbitrarily many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, one per label, and no others. The construction extends to $r$-uniform hypergraphs for every fixed $r\ge3$, yielding a GHZ dimension that grows at least polynomially as the number of paths ranges over the positive multiples of $r$.

papers.title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: The probabilistic nature of quantum computation can be an asset rather than an obstacle for combinatorial optimization. In this work, we tackle the problem in which the sampled distribution itself is the object being optimized. This perspective is especially natural for fairness, coverage, and robustness objectives, where success is determined by the least-protected components rather than by average or best performance. We develop this idea by learning graph cut distributions. The resulting framework turns Fair Cut Cover into a native quantum distribution-learning problem and uses quantum circuits as trainable generators of cut distributions. We prove that standard QAOA at depth one achieves higher Fair Cut Cover values than optimal Semidefinite programming plus Gaussian hyperplane rounding on complete graphs with at least four vertices. We further establish a separation on a family of high-girth graphs using published QAOA evaluations, compare against a classical column-generation heuristic in numerical experiments, and examine finite-sampling and noise effects in quantum hardware implementations. These results suggest a broader role for this type of quantum algorithms: not merely finding good bitstrings, but learning useful combinatorial distributions for worst- and average-case-aware optimization.

papers.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
papers.abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.

papers.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
papers.abstract: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients. For the deformed displacement chain the spread complexity is the mean excitation number, its rate is the deformed momentum quadrature, and its acceleration is $\ddot C_K=2\omega^2\langle[a,a^\dagger]\rangle$, so the deformed commutator acts as a force along the Krylov chain and the mean deformation controls early-time growth. The deformation parameters separate four regimes. For $\max(p,q)<1$ the complexity stays bounded, a localization produced by the algebra alone. For $p=1$, $q<1$ it grows ballistically, with an exact asymptotic velocity given by a theta-type series. At $p=q=1$ it grows as $t^2$. For $\max(p,q)>1$ the Jacobi operator is not essentially self-adjoint, the moment problem is indeterminate, and the Lanczos coefficients no longer determine the dynamics. Even and odd truncations converge to two different evolutions, the two reflection-symmetric N-extremal solutions of the moment problem, the odd one carrying a zero-energy atom of closed-form weight; the self-adjoint extensions yield a family of complexity curves that coincide at early times and separate once the Krylov wavefront reaches infinity. Krylov complexity in this regime is thus defined only once a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified. The orthogonal-polynomial procedure and its checks on exactly solvable chains are given in the appendices.

papers.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
papers.abstract: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

papers.title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
papers.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet we prove, at leading order, a d-wave inverse-square law, 1.376 times the spin-wave amplitude, a clover-shaped entangled region, exact without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term, and that each spin's entanglement is entirely pairwise. Four qubits can test the d-wave signs at present error rates.

papers.title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. (Quantum Theory from First Principles, 2017). Both of them refer to compound systems, the theory of which is rather directly assumed to be given by the tensor product structure. This structure, though well understood, should, however, be based on a more careful study of formal composition rules describing how local effects can be embedded into the compound effect space and how to reduce joint states onto subsystems. In that we follow the earlier work of T. Matolcsi, (Acta Sci. Math., 1975), and D. Aerts and I. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. We also establish axioms of local discrimination stating that compound states can be told apart by local measurements the notion of which we also formally define. The purification axioms first introduced as axioms of quantum mechanics by D'Ariano et al. are also rewritten in a weaker form which we believe could be fruitful for future axiomatizations. These reformulations bring us closer to proper tensor product structures for joint state and effect spaces, so that the embedding map for states factors through the projective tensor product of the local state spaces and the embedding map for effects factors through the injective tensor product of the local effect spaces. We also discuss the case of multipartite composition axioms and associativity properties required in these settings.

papers.title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
papers.abstract: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.
